correctness.rationale: Every dual tangent covering with <=8 lines has a full pencil, by exhaustive 7,888,725 eight-line incidence check. Every smooth quartic having such a full pencil is represented by one of 34,375 exhaustive rational contact configurations and hence by a solution of its 12 linear constraints. Exact GF(5) row reduction enumerates all nonzero solutions and excludes rationally nonsingular curves with <=8 rational points; this superset includes all geometrically smooth cases. Both nine-point witnesses have nine tangent lines covering all 31 rational points and three exact unit-gradient Groebner bases proving geometric smoothness. All standalone programs executed successfully.

value.rationale: The exact minimum number of rational tangent contact points for a smooth genus-three plane quartic over F5 is a motivated extremal invariant in the dual-blocking approach to tangent-filling. It is not implied by genus-three point counts, smooth-quartic existence, or the nontrivial blocking-set bound because full pencil configurations require exclusion. Sharp examples exhibit both pencil and nontrivial dual-blocking geometry; no downstream general theorem is required for this concrete structural boundary.
